concept.tagline: Combining shift-left ingestion contracts, Write-Audit-Publish (WAP) Iceberg branching, and statistical drift detection to quarantine bad data before publication.
concept.purpose: Build a progressive mental model of data quality engineering—from the 5 quality dimensions and deterministic vs statistical checks to WAP gates and partition-scoped SLIs.

spark.summary: Data quality checks validate schema, freshness, volume, distribution, and business invariants across ingestion and transformation stages so corrupted data is quarantined before reaching dashboards or ML models.
spark.keyTakeaway: Shift data quality left into CI/CD and ingestion contracts, and pair deterministic rule assertions with statistical anomaly detection and circuit-breaker quarantining.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** Data quality checks are automated assertions and statistical monitors placed at pipeline boundaries to verify datasets are **fit for purpose** across five dimensions: **completeness** (null rates), **uniqueness** (duplicate.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Hourly Iceberg WAP Gate Preventing Corrupt Data From Reaching BI (Kafka + Schema -> Spark Writer -> audit_* Branch -> Iceberg main); Iceberg Branch Audit & Promotion State Machine (STAGED BRANCH -> PUBLISHED MAIN -> QUARANTINED).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Pair deterministic SQL/contract tools with statistical observability rather than expecting one tool to cover everything. Every batch moves deterministically from staged write to audit evaluation, either atomically fast-forwarding `main` or halting on the audit branch while routing bad records to a monitored quarantine table.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore how DLQs, late-data watermarking, real-time Medallion lakehouses, and schema evolution work together with data quality gates.

learningJourney.title: What are Data Quality Checks (5 Dimensions & 3 Layers)
learningJourney.explanation:
Data quality checks are automated assertions and statistical monitors placed at pipeline boundaries to verify datasets are **fit for purpose** across five dimensions: **completeness** (null rates), **uniqueness** (duplicate keys), **validity** (regex/enum/range), **timeliness** (freshness lag), and **consistency** (referential & accounting invariants).

A mature architecture separates **structural contracts** (Avro/Protobuf at ingestion), **semantic invariants** (`net_amount == gross - discount`), and **statistical observability** (row-count z-scores, PSI/KS distribution drift).
learningJourney.purpose: The mechanism: understand how Data Quality Checks (5 Dimensions & 3 Layers) works from first principles.

learningJourney.title: Why Check-After-Publish Fails (and How Write-Audit-Publish Fixes It)
learningJourney.explanation: Silent data corruption—a timezone shift, duplicate Kafka offset, or SDK enum change—trains broken ML models and skews ARR reports long before infra alerts fire. Running tests *after* overwriting production tables creates a race condition where BI tools already consumed bad data. **Write-Audit-Publish (WAP)** stages writes in an isolated Iceberg branch, runs audits, and atomically fast-forwards `main` only on pass.

sectionDiagram.summary: Staging data on an isolated Iceberg branch eliminates the check-after-publish race condition.

ideas.title: Write-Audit-Publish on Daily Billing Mart
ideas.description: Duplicate Stripe webhooks inflated ARR by 8%. Implementing Iceberg WAP + dbt tests (`unique` on `invoice_id`, `net_amount == gross - discount`) kept failed runs on the staging branch and cut billing discrepancies to zero.

ideas.title: ML Feature Drift Detection in Fraud Scoring
ideas.description: An SDK changed `device_os_version` from `17.2` to `iOS 17.2`, defaulting the encoder to `UNKNOWN` and spiking false declines by 3.4%. Soda Core PSI (>0.2) and set-membership checks caught the schema-valid semantic drift in 15 minutes.

learningJourney.title: Where to Place Quality Gates (and Cost/Latency Guardrails)
learningJourney.explanation: Scope checks to incremental partitions or Iceberg snapshot diffs (`SELECT * FROM table.changes`) to keep audit latency under 30 seconds and avoid full-table warehouse scan bills.

benefits: Blocks malformed JSON/Avro payloads before they ever pollute Bronze storage.
costs: Validates single-record syntax only—cannot catch cross-row duplicates or volume drops.

comparison.choice: Transformation Boundary (WAP in dbt / Spark / Iceberg)
benefits: Verifies primary keys, accounting identities, and partition freshness before `main` swap.
costs: Requires severity tiering (`ERROR` halts vs `WARN` alerts) so minor nulls don't freeze dashboards.

benefits: Partition-scoped checks + HyperLogLog sketches are 10–100x cheaper.
costs: Running `COUNT(DISTINCT user_id)` over 5 years of history hourly explodes Snowflake/BigQuery spend.

learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.

learningJourney.title: How to manage Quarantine, Severity Tiers & Quality SLIs
learningJourney.explanation:
1. **Row Quarantine vs. Batch Halt**: For non-critical dimensions, tag bad rows with `_dq_error_reason` and route to a quarantine table; for financial ledgers, halt the batch.
2. **Monitor the DLQ**: Track **Bad Record Rate** (`quarantined_rows / total_rows`), **Time-to-Detect (TTD)**, and **Freshness SLO**—alert if >0.1% is quarantined so the DLQ never becomes a silent black hole.
3. **Seasonal Baselines**: Calibrate statistical volume/drift alerts against 28-day seasonal windows.

```sql
-- Partition-scoped Write-Audit-Publish (WAP) invariant check in dbt / Iceberg SQL
SELECT invoice_id, gross_cents, discount_cents, net_cents
FROM {{ ref('stg_billing_invoices') }}
WHERE _ingested_date = CURRENT_DATE
  AND (net_cents != gross_cents - discount_cents OR net_cents < 0);
-- Non-empty result triggers ERROR severity, blocking fast-forward to Iceberg main.
```

options.text: Asynchronous post-publish checks create a race condition where BI dashboards and ML jobs consume corrupted data before the alert fires
options.feedback: Correct: WAP isolates unverified writes on a staging branch and atomically promotes `main` only after checks pass.

options.text: Iceberg branches compress Parquet files 10x smaller than `main`
options.feedback: Branching is a metadata pointer isolation mechanism, not a compression algorithm.
